reason: Completed B1/B2/S1/S2 DEV+replication+lockbox campaign is retained as protocol/harness evidence but reclassified as construct-invalid for the headline stateful/effectful/long-lived Cognitive Core thesis. The taskset did not require multi-session state, forced external memory, meaningful effects, supersession cognition, or tool use; the substrate path also wrote the current prompt into memory before retrieving it. The lockbox is therefore consumed and non-diagnostic, not reusable.
observed_results: DEV B1=17/20 (85%), B2=16/20 (80%), S1=14/20 (70%), S2=14/20 (70%). Replication B1=S1=10/12 and B2=S2=9/12. Lockbox B1=7/8, B2=6/8, S1=6/8, S2=6/8. S1/B1 DEV latency ratio approximately 2.55x, violating frozen C_latency=0.20. Because the old S1 treatment injected redundant current-turn context, B1->S1 (-15pp) and B2->S2 (-10pp) are retained only as initial null/context-injection tax observations, not universal constants.
affected_metrics: Headline thesis remains untested. Old receipts remain valid measurements. Permanent protocol additions: every substrate DEV probe includes S0 (same-schema length-matched off-topic null); O1 supplies perfect recall of the full relevant set rather than answer selection; construct DEV includes bare B2 size control; evaluator distinguishes supported-correct/correct-abstention/confident-wrong using deterministic typed intent fields; pilot and final DEV samples must be distinct; S1-vs-S0 uses the same one-sided exact paired statistic as Phase D; replication is blocked until construct validity passes; a new lockbox may not be created until construct-valid DEV plus independent replication demonstrate the preregistered directional separation.
new_evaluation_source: gauntlets/substrate_construct/pilot-v1.json for calibration, followed by distinct gauntlets/substrate_construct/dev-v1.json. Replication is generated only after construct-valid DEV; no new lockbox exists until check_lockbox_creation_ready passes.

reason: Pre-pilot construct audit found O1 and S1 structurally identical on most task families because only long-history tasks had a background address space, and the initial filler vocabulary was non-neutral under the actual substring keyword scorer. Typed Intent formatting also lacked a pre-registered benchmark-defect rule.
observed_results: Before correction, O1/S1 retrieved the same record set on 36/43 non-long-history tasks; the original long-history filler could displace all oracle records. After correction, every construct task has a deterministic >=153,600-word background address-space proxy, filler is generated to have zero overlap under the actual `query_word in content` scorer, and the preflight test recovers the full oracle record set with S1 on sampled tasks from every family.
affected_metrics: O1-S1 is now interpretable as retrieval-system loss across all construct families. Typed string values are pre-registered as casefolded with collapsed whitespace; argument key sets remain exact and unexpected keys fail. Pilot O1 invalid-rate >10% is classified as BENCHMARK_DEFECT_REVISE_FORMAT, not construct invalidation. `check_construct_pilot_ready` / `--check-construct-pilot` enforce this before pilot/final interpretation.
new_evaluation_source: Refreshed deterministic pilot-v1/dev-v1 materialisations after the pre-pilot fixes; no pilot model run had occurred before these changes.
